# Task: Support property-to-property comparisons in Cypher WHERE clauses

## Problem

The Cypher query subset supported by `src/cypher/cypher.c` fails to parse a WHERE condition that compares one variable's property with another variable's property. The query aborts with `expected value at pos N` at the right-hand operand.

Examples that fail on the current code:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.name <> b.name RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
```

Property-to-literal comparisons already work and must keep working:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE b.file_path = 'demo.go' RETURN a.name, b.name
```

## Required behavior

Extend the WHERE parser and evaluator so that when the right-hand side of a comparison operator is another `variable.property` expression (not a string/number/boolean literal), the condition compares the two resolved property values for the current binding.

1. `a.prop = b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values are equal.
2. `a.prop <> b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values differ.
3. All existing comparison operators that make sense on property values (`>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`) should also accept a property right-hand side, evaluated the same way as when the right-hand side is a numeric literal (via `strtod`).
4. The property right-hand side must resolve through the same binding mechanism used for the left-hand side (`node_prop` / bare-alias name), so File, Function, and other node property paths all work.
5. Property-to-literal and bare-alias comparisons must continue to work exactly as before.
6. The change must work in both the early WHERE (after MATCH) and post-WITH WHERE paths, since they share the same parser and evaluator.

## Where to change

- Parser: `parse_condition_expr` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently rejects a non-literal right-hand side with `expected value at pos %d`.
- Condition model: `cbm_condition_t` in `src/cypher/cypher.h` currently only stores a literal `value`.
- Evaluator: `eval_condition` / `resolve_condition_value` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently resolve only the left-hand side against the binding.

## Constraints

- Do not break any existing Cypher behavior (WHERE with literals, regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT).
- Keep the error path for genuinely unsupported right-hand sides (e.g. function calls on the RHS if not already supported) clear and non-crashing.
- Add unit tests in the existing Cypher test suite covering property-to-property `=`, `<>`, and at least one ordering operator, plus a WITH-path case.
- The full project test suite (`make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test`) must still pass.

## How to verify

```sh
make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli index_repository '{"repo_path":"/tmp/demo","mode":"full","name":"demo"}'
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph '{"project":"demo","query":"MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name"}'
```

Before the fix this errors with `expected value at pos N`. After the fix it returns only CALLS edges whose source and target files are the same.

I’ll inspect the Cypher parser/model/evaluator and existing tests just enough to hand off implementation and independent verification with precise targets.The core structs and parser area are identified; I’m narrowing the handoff to the exact parser/evaluator/test touchpoints rather than changing code here.The evaluator uses a single `cbm_condition_t` LHS resolver and literal `value`; I’m checking the rest of condition evaluation plus locating the test suite before delegating.I have enough context for a surgical implementation handoff: update the condition AST to distinguish literal RHS from variable/property RHS, reuse existing binding resolution, and add Cypher tests.I’ll also queue an independent review focused on parser/evaluator compatibility and the requested regression coverage.**Delegated.** Implementation is assigned to `coder` with exact parser/model/evaluator/test requirements, and independent verification is queued for `reviewer` after implementation.

Key handoff points: extend `cbm_condition_t` to represent RHS `IDENT[.IDENT]`, parse it in `parse_condition_expr`, resolve it through the same binding path as the LHS in `eval_condition`, preserve all existing literal/operator behavior, and add tests for `=`, `<>`, ordering, post-`WITH` WHERE, and literal regression.

activities.objective: Implement support for property-to-property RHS comparisons in Cypher WHERE clauses. Target files: `src/cypher/cypher.h`, `src/cypher/cypher.c`, and the existing Cypher C test suite (locate current tests under the repo; prior attempts at `tests/test_cypher.c`/`tests/c/test_cypher.c` may not exist). Contract: `parse_condition_expr` currently only accepts literal RHS for comparison ops and errors with `expected value at pos N`; extend it so comparison RHS may be `IDENT[.IDENT]` representing a binding-backed RHS expression. Update `cbm_condition_t` to store RHS expression metadata separately from literal `value` (e.g. RHS variable/property and/or a flag) while preserving existing fields/behavior for literals, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, IN, IS NULL/NOT NULL, regex/string operators. Update `expr_free` and any WHERE cleanup paths to free new fields. Evaluation: in `eval_condition`, resolve RHS property/bare alias through the same binding mechanism as LHS (`resolve_condition_value`/binding logic, including nodes, edges, and post-WITH virtual aliases); then use the resolved RHS string as `expected` for `=`, `<>`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` and other existing comparison/string operators only where already accepted by parser. Numeric ordering must continue to use existing `strtod` comparison semantics. Preserve property-to-literal and bare-alias comparisons exactly. Unsupported RHS forms such as function calls must still fail clearly/non-crash. Both early WHERE after MATCH and post-WITH WHERE should work because they share parser/evaluator. Add unit tests in the existing Cypher test suite covering: `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN ...`; `a.name <> b.name`; at least one ordering op with property RHS (e.g. `a.start_line < b.start_line` or equivalent property available in fixtures); and a WITH-path case like `MATCH ... WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN ...`. Also keep/add a literal comparison assertion to guard no regression. Verify with the smallest relevant test target first, then run `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test` (or if too broad/fails for environmental reasons, report exact command/output and run `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm`).
